items.title: 68239_Ram Ramirez oral history interview
items.q: Gershwin was such an innovator. I mean, you just can't underplay his Rhapsody on the Blues, you know.

ctx.x: Some of J.P.'s accompaniment to singers I heard on the old-fashioned records, he would play something out of Gershwin)'s music, "Rhapsody In Blue" or something like that. But in his touch of blues, you hardly noticed it. But if you're familiar with the composition of "Rhapsody in Blue" or some of the parts of this... And Gershwin was vice-versa, too. He would do a lot of Johnson's... "A Woman Is A Sometime Thing", the opening of Porgy and Bess, I mean to me it's all Johnson with, of course, extra harmony added.…

I think you're making a very good point here. Because Chicago being spread out more, the thing wouldn't be integrated in the same way as it would in New York. Black and White were compelled to mingle by the island.
